setup: Sit upright with your back supported or lie flat on your back on a firm, comfortable surface.
Extend the target leg straight out in front of you with the toes pointing toward the ceiling.
Keep the other leg comfortably relaxed or bent at the knee.
steps: Contract the quadriceps muscles on the front of your thigh, pressing the back of your knee down toward the floor.
Focus on drawing your kneecap upward toward your hip as you sustain the contraction.
Hold the maximal voluntary contraction for the prescribed duration.
Gradually release the contraction and relax the thigh fully before starting the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and evenly throughout the hold; do not hold your breath during the isometric contraction.
cues: Press the back of the knee down
Pull your kneecap toward your hip

common_faults.fault: Holding the breath during the isometric hold
common_faults.correction: Maintain slow, steady breathing throughout each contraction.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the heel off the floor
common_faults.correction: Keep the heel resting on the surface; focus on pressing the knee downward rather than lifting the leg.

common_faults.fault: Overusing the gluteal or hamstring muscles instead of the quadriceps
common_faults.correction: Keep your buttocks relaxed and focus entirely on squeezing the muscles on the front of the thigh.

precautions: Perform smoothly without sharp, sudden contractions if recovering from acute knee surgery or injury

name: Quad Set
summary: An isometric knee extension exercise performed seated or supine to activate and strengthen the quadriceps muscles.
